questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ 1-{e}^{-x}, & x\ge 0,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(X>2).$
questions.worked_solution:
We can perform this computation using the complement, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>2) & =1-P(X\le 2) \\  & =1-F(2) \\  & =1-(1-{e}^{-2}) \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{64}x(16-{x}^{2}),\, & 0\le x\le 4 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<0 \\ h(x),\, & 0\le x\le 4 \\ 1,\, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability density function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $0<x<4,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 0\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{64}t(16-{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{1}{64}(8{t}^{2}-\frac{{t}^{4}}{4})|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{64}(8{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}) \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{256}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{256}, & 0\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ 1-\frac{1}{{x}^{6}}, & x\ge 1,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(X\le 2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

Hence, the required probability is $F(2)=1-\frac{1}{{2}^{6}}=\frac{63}{64}.$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-|5x|},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{5x}}{2},\, & x<0 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-5t}\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals.

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{5t}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{5x}}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{5x}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-5t}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-5t}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-5t}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{5x}}{2}, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{2}, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{9}x+\frac{8}{9},\, & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<1 \\ h(x),\, & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 1,\, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $1\le x\le 4,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ {\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{x}(-\frac{2}{9}t+\frac{8}{9})\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={(-\frac{1}{9}{t}^{2}+\frac{8}{9}t)|}_{1}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}{x}^{2}+\frac{8}{9}x-\frac{7}{9} \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}({x}^{2}-8x+7) \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}(x-1)(x-7).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ -\frac{1}{9}(x-1)(x-7), & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$
